Statistische Auswertung mit netzwerkbasierten Vergleichen und Bootstrap-Konfidenzintervallen. Explorative Sensitivitäts- und Robustheitsanalysen. Prospektiv spezifizierte explorative Folgeuntersuchung X3 mit einer beobachtungsbasierten Korrekturstrategie und einem Orakel-Vergleichsmaßstab. Dokumentation der Reproduzierbarkeit einschließlich ausführbarem Code und ergänzenden Prüfmaterialien. Zentrale Ergebnisse 1. Stabilität bedeutet nicht Richtigkeit.Ein Rückkopplungssystem kann ein stabiles Gleichgewicht erreichen, obwohl seine kollektive Entscheidung systematisch falsch bleibt. 2. Gemeinsame Fehler können grundsätzlich nicht identifizierbar sein.Wenn alle zugänglichen Informationskanäle dieselbe unbekannte Verzerrung enthalten, lässt sich diese unter den definierten Annahmen nicht allein durch interne Beobachtungen vom tatsächlichen Zustand unterscheiden. 3. Fehlererkennung garantiert keine Korrigierbarkeit.Auch ein identifizierter Fehler kann außerhalb der Korrekturmöglichkeiten der verfügbaren Stellgrößen liegen. 4. Einfluss kann entscheidender sein als zahlenmäßige Mehrheiten.Im simulierten Modell verursachte eine einflussreiche Minderheit größere Entscheidungsfehler als eine zahlenmäßig größere Mehrheit mit geringerem Einfluss. 5. Korrekturmechanismen können Fehler verstärken.Audits mit verzerrten oder kompromittierten Referenzen können schlechter abschneiden als ein System ohne Audit. 6. title: Membentuk Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Sinergi Digital Entrepreneurship, Persepsi Harga dan Kualitas Produk Studi Pada Konsumen Jatinangor House Kota Bogor
summary: This study aims to analyze and determine 1) The Influence of Digital Entrepreneurship on Purchase Decisions, 2) The Influence of Price Perception on Purchase Decisions, 3) The Influence of Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City. The development of a competitive culinary industry in the digital economy era requires business actors to integrate technology and maintain product value alignment in order to influence consumer behavior. The type of research used is a quantitative approach with a survey method. Primary data collection was conducted through the distribution of structured questionnaires with a Likert scale to 180 respondents selected using non-probability sampling technique with a purposive sampling approach, which is a sampling technique based on certain criteria established by the researcher. The criteria for respondents are Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City who have made a product purchase. The data analysis method used in this research is Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) through the Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis tool with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0 software. The results of hypothesis testing show that: 1) Digital Entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 3.021 and a p-value of 0.003, 2) Price Perception has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 1.988 and a p-value of 0.047, and finally 3) Product Quality has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 6.493 and a p-value of 0.000 The results of this study show that the variables of Digital Entrepreneurship, Price Perception, and Product Quality have a positive and significant influence on the Purchase Decisions of Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City. Product Quality is proven to be the variable that has the most dominant influence on the Purchase Decisions of Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City.

title: The Relationship between the Integration of Artificial Intelligence Technologies into Communication Strategies within Public Relations Departments and the Building of Government Institutional Reputation During Crises
summary: Public relations departments play a pivotal role in building institutional reputation and reinforcing the positive image of official organizations through effective communication with the media, identifying the current and future needs of stakeholders, strengthening internal organizational communication, and leveraging modern communication technologies to ensure rapid outreach, greater efficiency, and enhanced communication effectiveness. The significance of these responsibilities becomes even more pronounced during crises and emergency situations, which impose additional demands on public relations departments to address challenges and manage circumstances that may adversely affect the organization's reputation, thereby requiring sustained efforts to protect, preserve, and enhance that reputation under exceptional conditions. This, in turn, necessitates the adoption of appropriate communication strategies capable of supporting institutional reputation during crises while ensuring their effectiveness in reducing public anxiety, particularly amid political and social tensions and rapidly changing environments. Furthermore, the design and implementation of these communication strategies should take into account the prevailing cultural and social contexts to maximize the effectiveness of communication processes and achieve their intended objectives. In this context, public relations departments within government institutions increasingly adopt comprehensive, integrated, and diversified communication strategies during crises, whereby the efforts of public relations practitioners are coordinated within a unified strategic framework. Such strategies should be characterized by clarity, accuracy, consistency, and flexibility, while being derived from broader strategic plans shared across government entities to promote institutional coordination and encourage constructive engagement with all segments of society. Moreover, in light of digital transformation and the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence applications, it has become imperative for public relations departments to integrate these advanced technologies into their communication practices to meet the demands of the contemporary communication environment, expand organizational reach and influence, and strengthen institutional reputation, particularly during periods of crisis and uncertainty.

title: AUDITING STANDARDS, PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES, AND THE REDUCTION OF THE AUDIT EXPECTATION GAP: A QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS.
summary: The audit expectation gap remains a significant concern in the accounting profession, arising from differences between what users of financial statements expect auditors to accomplish and the responsibilities auditors are professionally required to perform. Audited financial statements provide investors, shareholders, creditors, and other stakeholders with reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and fair presentation of an organisation's financial information. Auditors also contribute to accountability, transparency, regulatory compliance, and the reliability of financial reporting. However, users of financial statements often perceive auditing as providing absolute assurance, whereas auditing professionals are primarily responsible for expressing an independent opinion on whether financial statements are free from material misstatements. These differing perceptions create expectations that may exceed the actual scope and limitations of an audit. This study examines the role of auditing standards and audit firms in reducing the audit expectation gap, with particular emphasis on professional responsibilities, audit quality, stakeholder awareness, and the reliability of financial reporting. Adopting a qualitative research approach, the study explores the contributions of established auditing standards, professional guidelines, and audit firm practices towards clarifying auditors' responsibilities and improving public understanding of the audit process. The study highlights the importance of effective communication between auditors and financial statement users, continuous professional development, compliance with auditing standards, and improved transparency in audit engagements. It further emphasises that audit firms and standard-setting institutions have complementary responsibilities in narrowing the gap between public expectations and actual audit performance. The study concludes that strengthening auditing standards, improving audit firm practices, and promoting stakeholder education are essential strategies for reducing the audit expectation gap, enhancing confidence in audited financial statements, and sustaining public trust in the auditing profession.

title: Data Governance and Ethical Issues in Accounting Technology
summary: Purpose: The introduction of advanced technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems has transformed accounting practices, allowing for quicker processing, greater transparency, and more informed decision-making. Despite these benefits, they also bring up crucial concerns related to data governance and ethical responsibility. This paper explores how governance frameworks and ethical standards can be applied to ensure trust, adherence to regulations, and integrity in technology-driven accounting settings. Methodology: This study utilizes a conceptual and case-based approach, referencing regulatory frameworks such as IFRS, Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), GDPR, and the EU AI Act. It addresses ethical challenges like bias in AI predictions, transparency in disclosures, risks of fraud in digital records, and responsibility for technology-driven mistakes. Case studies, including ERP breaches revealing client information, incorrect reporting of crypto assets due to a lack of standards, and inaccuracies in ESG reporting, are analyzed to demonstrate real-world issues. Findings: The research finds that strong data governance ensures accuracy, integrity, and compliance, while ethical oversight protects stakeholder trust. Weak governance leaves organizations vulnerable to cybersecurity threats, harm to reputation, and regulatory fines. Excessive reliance on automation without professional skepticism weakens ethical judgment, while emerging areas such as ESG reporting and blockchain require new accountability frameworks. The findings highlight that accountants must transition from traditional record keepers to digital stewards of trust. Implications: The paper suggests practical strategies, including forming AI governance councils, performing regular audits for bias and security, and incorporating ESG metrics into accounting systems. It advocates for a balanced approach where innovation aligns with compliance and ethics, ensuring that technology bolsters rather than compromises financial integrity. By embedding governance and ethical principles into accounting technology, organizations can enhance stakeholder trust and create resilient financial systems.

title: Electronic Governance as a Tool for Ensuring the Continuity of Public Services During a Crisis Period
summary: Purpose: To examine electronic governance as a mechanism for ensuring the continuity of public service delivery during crises and to evaluate the capacity of digital government systems to maintain services when conventional face-to-face delivery is disrupted. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study uses an integrative literature review of eight open-access studies (n = 8) published between 2020 and 2025, identified through a search of academic databases and journal websites in March 2026. The selected publications were screened against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and coded by context, evidence type, digital mechanisms, and contribution to service continuity; the coded data were examined through qualitative thematic synthesis. Research Limitation: The review is limited to published literature and does not include primary empirical evidence. Future studies should validate these findings through comparative and quantitative research. Findings: Electronic governance supports service continuity through rapid organisational adaptation, legal and procedural continuity in government–citizen interactions, and increased citizen adoption of digital services when systems are transparent and accessible. Crises also accelerate digital transformation by reducing bureaucratic resistance, although legal constraints, digital exclusion, and unequal administrative capacity remain important challenges. Practical Implication: The findings guide the development of resilient digital governance systems that can maintain uninterrupted public services during emergencies. Social Implication: Effective electronic governance improves access to public services, strengthens citizen trust, and enhances institutional resilience. Originality/Value: The study presents an integrated framework explaining how electronic governance supports continuity and resilience of public service systems during crises.

title: The AI augmentation gap: data richness, automation and business value
summary: Purpose Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how data richness, as an organisational resource, is associated with business value through two deployment processes, automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled augmentation, and whether they differ in their capacity to generate value. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 366 Greek firms across four sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped mediation analysis and coefficient-difference tests; business value is measured as perceived value from digital technology. Findings Data richness is positively associated with both deployment processes. Automation is positively associated with business value and channels part of the association between data richness and value, whereas AI-enabled augmentation, the less developed process, shows no significant direct association; the difference is statistically significant, revealing an AI augmentation gap. Data richness also retains a significant direct association with value, and additional analyses suggest that the capability associations with value run through enacted digital transformation. Practical implications Firms should build a strategically governed data foundation, expand automation for near-term returns and develop augmentation as a longer-term capability built on skills, role redesign, validation and trust in AI-supported decisions; EuroMed policy instruments can be aligned with this sequencing. Originality/value Drawing on the RBV, the study shows that deployment processes of the same digital resource differ significantly in their association with value, a heterogeneity interpreted as reflecting the maturity of the complementary capabilities each requires, and provides evidence from a resource-constrained Mediterranean economy.

title: Cooperation stability and bistability in green innovation consortia
summary: Abstract Sustained cooperation in green innovation consortia depends on the incentives of governments, leading enterprises and knowledge-contributing members. This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game of institutional optimization, resource integration and deep participation. The payoff matrix yields three actor-specific cost ceilings for local stability of full cooperation. Under an illustrative baseline with uniformly positive enterprise and member margins, an analytical argument establishes convergence from every strictly interior initial state. Numerical integration of 125 initial states per scenario reproduces full cooperation and three stable partial-cooperation configurations under separate cost increases. Local stability does not, however, guarantee attraction from arbitrary initial states: with other baseline parameters fixed, full cooperation and enterprise-only active integration coexist for member participation costs between 60 and 160. At a cost of 150, different initial shares approach different corners. Parameter sweeps further distinguish changes in adjustment trajectories from changes in stability and attraction; both cost and return parameters can affect cooperative configurations. These theoretical findings support diagnosis of actor-specific payoff margins and initial cooperation conditions, while leaving empirical calibration, environmental outcomes and optimal policy allocation for future research.

title: Le contrôle de gestion augmenté : quand l'intelligence artificielle repense le pilotage des universités publiques. Revue de littérature et perspectives pour le Maroc
summary: RésuméLes universités publiques évoluent dans un environnement marqué par la transformation digitale, la pression budgétaire et l’exigence croissante de redevabilité. Dans ce contexte, le contrôle de gestion, longtemps cantonné à un rôle de mesure a posteriori, est appelé à se réinventer sous l’effet de l’intelligence artificielle (IA). Cet article analyse la manière dont l’IA transforme les dispositifs de contrôle de gestion et dans quelle mesure elle peut devenir un levier de performance pour les universités publiques.Il s’articule autour de la problématique suivante : dans quelle mesure l’intégration des outils d’intelligence artificielle transforme-t-elle les pratiques de contrôle de gestion et contribue-t-elle à l’amélioration de la performance des universités publiques ? Sur le plan méthodologique, l’étude repose sur une revue de littérature narrative et analytique, conduite à partir de bases de données académiques reconnues (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar) et organisée selon quatre axes : budgétaire, pédagogique, scientifique et gouvernance.Les résultats montrent que l’IA agit comme un levier de transformation du contrôle de gestion à travers l’automatisation des processus, l’amélioration de la qualité de l’information, le renforcement des capacités prédictives et l’appui à la décision stratégique. Son intégration se heurte toutefois à des contraintes institutionnelles, organisationnelles et éthiques, et fait persister une tension entre logiques académiques et logiques de performance. L’article propose des pistes pour une intégration contextualisée et responsable de l’IA dans les universités publiques, en particulier marocaines.Mots-clés : contrôle de gestion, intelligence artificielle, performance universitaire, secteur public, transformation digitale, enseignement supérieur, Maroc. AbstractPublic universities operate in an environment shaped by digital transformation, budgetary pressure and growing demands for accountability. In this context, management control, long confined to an after-the-fact measurement role, is being reshaped by artificial intelligence (AI). This paper examines how AI transforms management control systems and to what extent it can become a performance lever for public universities.It addresses the following research question: to what extent does the integration of AI tools transform management control practices and contribute to improving the performance of public universities? Methodologically, the study relies on a narrative and analytical literature review drawing on recognized academic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar), organized around four axes: budget, teaching, research and governance.The findings show that AI acts as a lever for transforming management control through process automation, improved information quality, stronger predictive capabilities and support for strategic decision-making. However, its integration remains constrained by institutional, organizational and ethical barriers, and a tension persists between academic logics and performance logics. The paper offers avenues for a contextualized and responsible integration of AI in public universities, with particular attention to the Moroccan context.Keywords : management control, artificial intelligence, university performance, public sector, digital transformation, higher education, Morocco.

title: The Mix-Match Concept of Digital Supply Chain and Digital Sustainability Practices
summary: The efficient management of global operations and supply chain (SC) flows has become crucial for organisations seeking to achieve operational efficiency, process optimisation, flexibility, and sustainable long-term growth in today's dynamic and linked business environment. This study places a greater emphasis on I4.0 (I4.0) and the technologies it offers, which are particularly beneficial for SC, smart manufacturing and sustainability. I4.0 and its associated technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), big data analytics, cloud computing, and blockchain technology, offer significant benefits for enhancing business optimisation and streamlining labour processes. Enhancing SC networks through the implementation of I4.0 technologies has demonstrated notable improvements, particularly in the field of industrial engineering. Identifying potential risks associated with the process of digitisation is a crucial aspect within an organisational context. The research employed a pragmatic philosophical framework, an inductive methodological approach, and thematic analysis to enhance the quality of the findings. This analysis examines the countries and firms that are at the forefront of global leadership. Additionally, it explores the significance of university partnerships in fostering innovation and driving commercial growth. A digital twin is used for problem-solving purposes, such as network design, decision-making, and the resolution of complicated operational issues. The implementation of organisational strategies can lead to enhanced operational efficiency, reduced risk exposure, and adept responsiveness to market dynamics, so contributing to a more promising future.

title: Pharmaceutical supply chain procurement strategies: group or decentralized
summary: As drug expenditures continue to rise, healthcare systems face growing pressure to improve procurement efficiency and control supply costs. Using game theory, this study identifies optimal procurement strategies for each stakeholder in the pharmaceutical supply chain, depending on market size, discount levels, and the group purchasing organisation’s (GPO) bargaining power. Specifically, medical institutions tend to engage in group procurement to aggregate demand in smaller markets, while in larger markets, they favour diversified strategies to maintain sourcing flexibility. The pharmaceutical manufacturer is more likely to adopt low-discount group procurement in both small and large markets, but shifts towards diversified procurement under medium or high discounts to maximise profits. A further comparison between decentralised and group procurement, with the manufacturer remaining the leader and the decision sequence unchanged, shows that medical institutions benefit more from group procurement as discounts strengthen. However, the manufacturer benefits only when demand expansion and economies of scale offset price concessions. Moreover, GPO bargaining power emerges as a pivotal factor that can alter the game’s dynamics, with its relative strength or weakness even capable of reversing the strategic choices of both buyers and suppliers. Managerial implications for medical institutions and pharmaceutical manufacturers regarding their procurement strategy are discussed. This study offers practical guidance for medical institutions, pharmaceutical manufacturers, and group purchasing organisations (GPOs) on improving pharmaceutical procurement decisions. The findings show that the most effective purchasing approach depends on market size, manufacturer discounts, and GPOs’ bargaining power. Medical institutions should assess these conditions before choosing between purchasing directly from manufacturers and purchasing through a GPO. In smaller markets, working with a GPO can help institutions combine demand and obtain better prices. Institutions should also evaluate a GPO’s bargaining strength and, importantly, whether the savings achieved by the GPO are passed on to them through lower prices or better contract terms. Pharmaceutical manufacturers can improve profitability by adapting their discount policies to different market conditions. Manufacturers should also strengthen their negotiating capabilities and diversify sales channels when dealing with powerful GPOs. GPOs can create greater value by expanding their purchasing scale, developing negotiation and market-analysis expertise, and designing contracts that reflect differences among participating institutions. Finally, coordination mechanisms such as two-part tariff contracts, with appropriately designed membership fees and commissions, can help manufacturers and medical institutions share benefits more effectively and support stable, long-term supply-chain relationships.

title: Mapping the evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research through bibliometric analysis
summary: The intensifying implications of climate change have brought carbon accounting and disclosure to the forefront of policy and scholarly debate, generating an emerging research field that examines its multidimensional nature. Despite the growing body of literature, existing studies remain fragmented and fail to provide a consolidated understanding of the field’s development. This research addresses that gap by conducting a bibliometric examination of 715 Scopus-indexed articles published between 1992 and 2025. Using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer, the study uncovers prominent publication trends, leading authors, and thematic trajectories in carbon accounting research. The results reveal a consistent increase in scholarly output over time, with China identified as the highest contributing nation and journals such as the Journal of Cleaner Production and Sustainability (Switzerland) recognized as the most productive publishing outlets. The most productive author is found to be Professor Tang Q of Western Sydney University. Thematic mapping and co-occurrence analysis highlight six dominant research clusters: Corporate Environmental Disclosure and Performance; Life Cycle and Emission Analysis; Climate Policy and Forest Carbon Sequestration; Technological and Emerging Themes in Carbon Management; Accounting and Methodological Approaches; and Carbon Disclosure, Sustainability, and Regional Empirical Synthesis. This study provides valuable insights into the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research, while offering directions for future inquiry and informing policy discussions in the field.

title: Integrating Talent Management and Public Service Innovation through an Innovation Pool: A Conceptual Model in the Illustrative Context of the Regional Civil Service Agency of South Sulawesi Province
summary: Digital transformation, rising public expectations and increasingly complex public problems require local governments to develop a competent, adaptive, collaborative and innovative Indonesian State Civil Apparatus (ASN) workforce. Talent management in the public sector therefore needs to move beyond staffing, succession and competency development towards identifying and mobilising individual capabilities to address organisational challenges, foster innovation and create public value. This article develops a conceptual model that integrates ASN talent management with public service innovation, using the Regional Civil Service Agency of South Sulawesi Province as an illustrative context. It adopts a qualitative, context sensitive conceptual model development design, drawing on an integrative literature review, an analysis of ASN talent management policies and a synthesis of four perspectives: strategic talent management, dynamic capabilities, public service motivation and public sector innovation. The resulting model comprises five interrelated dimensions: evidence-based talent mapping; innovation-oriented competency development; strategic talent placement and mobility; innovation leadership and collaborative culture; and evaluation of public service impacts. Its principal conceptual contribution is the innovation pool, a mechanism linking the talent pool to public service problem-solving by mobilising personnel according to the competency requirements of organisational innovation priorities. Implementation is supported by integrated personnel data, merit-based governance, transformational leadership, digitalisation and organisational learning. The model offers a strategic framework for aligning talent management and public service innovation to translate ASN capabilities into public value. As the literature was selected purposively rather than through a systematic review, empirical research is needed to assess the model's relevance, feasibility and applicability across different local government settings.

title: The Effect of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) on Profitability, with Liquidity as an Intervening Variable, in the Mining Sector During the Economic Transition Period (2021–2025)
summary: This study aims to analyze the impact of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) on profitability, with liquidity as an intervening variable, within the mining sector during the economic transition period of 2021–2025. The research is motivated by inconsistencies in previous studies regarding the relationships between CSR, liquidity, and profitability. A quantitative approach is employed, grounded in stakeholder theory. Using purposive sampling, 23 mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange—which publish sustainability reports in accordance with GRI standards—were selected, resulting in 115 observations. CSR is measured using the GRI disclosure index (CSRDI), liquidity via the Current Ratio (CR), and profitability through Return on Assets (ROA). Data were analyzed using linear regression and bootstrapping in SmartPLS 4, supplemented by classical assumption testing and HC3 standard error correction. The results indicate that CSR has a significant negative effect on the Current Ratio (CR). The CR has a positive but statistically insignificant effect on ROA, while CSR also shows a positive but insignificant effect on ROA. The indirect effect of CSR on ROA through the CR is significant but negative, whereas the total effect is statistically insignificant. Consequently, all proposed hypotheses are rejected. These findings suggest that CSR functions as a long-term investment, which, in the short term, consumes cash without yet enhancing profitability. The very low R² value indicates that numerous factors outside the model influence ROA.

title: THE IMPACT OF ESG (ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, GOVERNANCE) CRITERIA ON FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENTS
summary: In the modern globalized economy, the determinants of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) have shifted beyond traditional financial metrics and macroeconomic indicators. International institutional investors and multinational enterprises (MNEs) increasingly incorporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria into their cross-border investment strategies. This study examines the structural mechanism through which country-level and firm-level ESG compliance influences inward FDI flows. The paper analyzes the individual contribution of the three ESG pillars, emphasizing that while strong governance ($G$) serves as a foundational prerequisite for risk mitigation, robust environmental ($E$) policies and social ($S$) capital significantly enhance long-term sustainability and operational stability. The findings demonstrate that high ESG standards lower systemic risk premiums, foster regulatory alignment, and create a sustainable environment for cross-border capital reallocation.

title: From Soccer Fields to Digital Wallets: How Green Fintech Can Bridge Gender Gaps in Rural Sports Development
summary: This review explores the potential of green fintech to reduce the existing gender gap in rural-based sports, primarily soccer. This multidisciplinary narrative review brings together literature on barriers to women's sports participation, digital financial inclusion, and environmental sustainability. Financial limitations, scarce infrastructure, and sociocultural constraints emerge as relevant concerns across these fields. Green fintech offers possible financing and delivery mechanisms, although evidence of its effects on rural women's sports participation remains limited. The study develops a conceptual framework linking stakeholder collaboration, green finance, accessible technology, and coordinated policy. Proposed applications include community finance, public–private partnerships, sponsorship, and NGO-supported initiatives. These applications are analytical propositions rather than evaluated cases or demonstrated outcomes. Regulatory barriers and digital divides may restrict implementation. Future research should test whether specific interventions improve access, sustained participation, and environmental performance in rural sport settings.

title: Do Investors Sanction Greenwashing? Selective Market Discipline in Fintech Firms
summary: ABSTRACT We investigate whether stock market investors detect and penalise greenwashing. We draw on media reports of environmental, social and governance incidents at 321 US‐listed fintech firms between 2007 and 2025, within which greenwashing is identified, following RepRisk, as misleading communication about environmental practice. Investors impose no measurable price penalty when firms are publicly implicated in greenwashing, and the sample is large enough to have detected a penalty of the size observed for other conduct. Misleading communication that does not concern the environment is penalised, where cumulative abnormal returns are between 0.4% and 0.6% lower over the 2 weeks following the report, falling further to 0.8% over the 4 weeks before and after, whereas physical environmental damage draws no adverse reaction. The market therefore prices dishonesty, but the sanction depends on the domain of the false claim, and environmental claims by fintech firms fall outside it. Consistent with stakeholder theory, the results suggest that market‐based discipline exists but is selective, so that the truthfulness of environmental claims cannot be presumed to be enforced by investors where regulatory oversight is absent.

title: Digital transformation of Pegadaian’s gold pawn services as a strategy to enhance financial inclusion and MSME competitiveness
summary: Background: Digital transformation in the financial services sector has become a strategic approach to enhancing financial inclusion and micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSME) competitiveness, particularly through non-bank institutions offering asset-based financing. In Indonesia, Pegadaian’s digital gold pawn services provide an accessible financial instrument for unbanked and underbanked communities. However, the role of digitalized pawn-based services in strengthening MSME competitiveness through financial inclusion mechanisms remains insufficiently explored. Methods: This study employs a qualitative descriptive approach using a systematic literature review of academic publications, policy documents, and institutional reports. The analysis integrates the frameworks of digital transformation, financial inclusion, and MSME capability development to synthesize empirical findings into a coherent analytical narrative. Findings: Digital gold pawn services expand access to formal financing, improve service transparency, accelerate transactions, and enhance financing predictability. Their contribution to financial inclusion extends beyond initial access to sustained usage and improved service quality. For MSMEs, competitiveness benefits primarily arise from liquidity stabilization, cost efficiency, temporal flexibility, and gradual capability development rather than immediate growth acceleration. Digital pawn services also help MSMEs manage cash flow volatility, reduce reliance on high-cost informal lenders, and foster financial discipline through repeated digital engagement. Conclusion: Pegadaian’s digital transformation represents a context-sensitive, capability-enhancing strategy that connects financial inclusion with sustainable MSME competitiveness. Its contribution is particularly evident in improving access to asset-based financing and supporting more effective financial management among underserved business communities. Novelty/Originality of this article: This study offers an integrated institutional perspective on digital gold pawn services as a non-bank, asset-based financing pathway linking digital transformation, financial inclusion, and MSME competitiveness. By examining these dimensions within an emerging market context, it extends the discussion of digital financial services beyond conventional banking and fintech models to highlight the potential role of digitalized pawn-based financing in sustainable MSME development.

title: Supply chain networks in horticulture: an assessment of farmers' perceptions and market linkages
summary: Purpose This study investigates the determinants of horticulture supply chain efficiency (SCE) and the mediating effects of market linkage strength (MLS). Design/methodology/approach The study conceptualises and tests a partial least squares structural equation modelling model based on the resource-based view and relational exchange theory, with the data collected from 500 horticultural farmers from Shimla, Kullu and Kinnaur districts of Himachal Pradesh. Findings The findings show that logistics capability (LC) has the strongest effects on MLS (β = 0.395) and SCE (β = 0.388), followed by information and coordination (IC). Transaction fairness (TF) and digital adoption (DA) significantly strengthen MLS, while MLS positively influences SCE (β = 0.233). MLS provides complementary mediation for LC and IC and indirect-only mediation for TF and DA. Originality/value The study integrates operational capabilities and relational mechanisms to explain how market linkages contribute to horticultural supply-chain efficiency, offering context-specific evidence from an underexplored horticultural setting.

title: Business and Revenue Models of the Metaverse in Indonesia's Digital Economy
summary: This paper examines the business and revenue models of the metaverse and assesses their viability within Indonesia's digital economy. Its purpose is to move the discussion beyond promotional forecasts by asking how value is actually created, delivered, and captured in immersive virtual environments, and which of those mechanisms fit Indonesian market conditions. The study applies a literature review combined with an analysis of public data and documented Indonesian cases, using the Business Model Canvas and revenue model typologies as analytical frames. The literature synthesis identifies seven revenue mechanisms: sales of virtual goods and non-fungible tokens, virtual real estate, advertising and brand experiences, subscriptions and paid access, gaming and play to earn mechanics, business to business services such as training and digital twins, and platform commissions on third party transactions. The Indonesian case analysis covers Telkom's metaNesia platform, the Nusameta ecosystem developed by WIR Group together with state owned banks BRI, BNI, and Mandiri, and the social metaverse Jagat. The results show that Indonesia possesses strong demand side fundamentals, including 221.56 million internet users in 2024 and the largest digital economy in Southeast Asia, yet the revenue models that stalled were those dependent on speculative asset sales and headset based immersion, while models anchored in business services, brand marketing budgets, and mobile first social experiences proved more durable. The novelty of this study lies in mapping each global revenue mechanism onto Indonesian readiness factors and documented local cases, producing a viability ordering that managers and policymakers can use when deciding where metaverse investment in Indonesia is commercially defensible and where it remains speculative.

title: Recruitment Tasks and Skill Requirements across Healthcare Supply-Chain Stages in China
summary: Abstract How do recruitment tasks and skill requirements evolve across healthcare supply chains? We examine online job advertisements from China's pharmaceutical and medical-device manufacturing and distribution sectors in 2015--2022. A common text-classification framework distinguishes advertised tasks, skills and formal requirements, enabling annual comparisons across four supply-chain segments. A descriptive decomposition separates changes within segments from changes in their representation in the observed advertisements. Recruitment profiles differ across stages, and these differences evolve over time. In the later period, pharmaceutical manufacturers advertised sales and market-development tasks more often than distributors, while distributors more often requested scientific and medical knowledge and advertised quality, regulatory, clinical and technical-service work. Medical-device recruitment followed different trajectories, showing that stage differences depend on product category and year. The pooled increase in scientific-and-medical-knowledge requirements arose from changes within the four segments, with changes in segment composition slightly offsetting that increase. The study provides a consistent framework for comparing recruitment content across healthcare industries and identifies supply-chain position as an additional dimension of heterogeneity in advertised labour demand. These findings show how industry averages can conceal distinct recruitment trajectories across manufacturing and distribution.

title: ESG Controversies and Short‐Term Profitability: The Role of Current ESG Performance and Lagged Reputation in Emerging Markets
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether ESG controversy involvement is associated with short‐term return on equity (ROE) and whether current and lagged ESG scores moderate that relationship among Indian nonfinancial firms. Drawing on stakeholder theory, legitimacy theory, and the managerial opportunism hypothesis, the study analyses 382 NIFTY 500 firm‐year observations for FY2024–25 using Hayes PROCESS Macro moderation models, with PLS‐SEM employed as a robustness check. ESG controversy involvement is positively associated with ROE, an association consistent with transitory cost externalization under India's formative mandatory disclosure environment. Current ESG scores significantly attenuate the controversy–ROE association, with positive associations concentrated among low‐ESG firms rather than consistently observed across all firms, providing conditional support for the managerial opportunism hypothesis. This moderating pattern is corroborated across estimation approaches. In contrast, ESG scores measured one and 2 years prior do not exhibit consistent additional moderation beyond current ESG performance. As controversy involvement and ROE are observed only for FY2024–25, the findings do not establish temporal adjustment, persistence, or changes in the financial consequences of controversies over time. The study contributes by distinguishing the moderating roles of current and prior ESG standing, identifying the conditional nature of the controversy–profitability association among NIFTY 500 non‐financial firms, and extending the managerial opportunism hypothesis to an emerging‐market regulatory context.

title: Automation in Accounting and its Opportunities and Challenges.
summary: Accounting automation is increasingly transforming the way organizations manage their financial activities. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Machine Learning, and cloud-based accounting systems has changed traditional accounting practices. These technologies enable organizations to process financial information more efficiently while reducing repetitive manual work and improving the quality and timeliness of financial information. This study examines the role of accounting automation in modern accounting practices, with particular emphasis on its impact on efficiency, accuracy, financial reporting, compliance, productivity, and the changing role of accountants. The study follows a descriptive research design and is based entirely on secondary data collected from academic journals, research papers, industry reports, and professional literature. The findings indicate that automation is increasingly being used for invoice processing, expense management, bank reconciliation, payment processing, data entry, payroll, and financial reporting. The study finds that accounting automation can reduce processing time, minimize human errors, lower operational costs, improve fraud detection, enhance compliance, and provide real-time financial information. However, challenges such as high implementation costs, cybersecurity risks, data privacy concerns, skill gaps, employee resistance, integration difficulties, and concerns about job displacement remain significant. The study concludes that accounting automation should complement rather than completely replace human expertise. Accountants need to develop technological, analytical, and strategic skills to remain relevant in an increasingly digital accounting environment.

title: Flow survival, maritime restoration, and commercial substitution: an empirical assessment of resilience in LNG supply-chain continuity during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption
summary: Sustainable energy supply chains depend on the assumption that resilience and sustainability move together. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption tests that assumption directly. For Qatar, a single-route LNG exporter with no pipeline bypass, the disruption produced a severe physical and logistical shock alongside a measurable macroeconomic one: QatarEnergy’s leadership estimated $20 billion in annual lost revenue (approximately 37% of expected government revenue), while Q1 2026 GDP contracted 7% year-on-year, driven by a 26% collapse in mining and quarrying. Existing quantitative treatments operate at the macroeconomic level, modeling cascading impacts on importing economies or generic blockade scenarios, but none empirically measures the exporting system’s resilience using verified, disaggregated flow, shipping, and contract data, or links that performance to its socio-economic and environmental consequences. This study addresses that gap through a multi-level empirical case analysis of QatarEnergy’s LNG export system (from 28 February 2026 through August 2026), distinguishing chokepoint-level operating conditions from a documented firm-level commercial response. Three resilience dimensions are operationalized as ex-post empirical proxies adapted from the absorptive-adaptive-restorative capacity framework: a flow-survival ratio (EIA tanker-tracking data), a maritime restoration proxy (daily vessel-transit observations), and a commercial substitution ratio (a buyer-level force-majeure and replacement sequence), reported primarily by volume and secondarily by cargo count. Results show LNG flow survival (approximately 8% of pre-war baseline) was substantially more severe than oil flow survival (approximately 23%), consistent with Qatar’s structural absence of pipeline bypass capacity. Maritime activity remained a small fraction of pre-war levels throughout, while volume-based commercial substitution for a major European buyer rose from 46% to a plateau of roughly 53% of canceled gas-equivalent volume, materially below the 72% implied by a cargo-count ratio for the same case. These findings indicate that physical, logistical, and commercial-adaptive resilience are empirically distinct dimensions, measured at different levels, that should be reported separately; even partial commercial substitution may mask, rather than resolve, underlying physical vulnerability whose socio-economic and environmental consequences persist regardless of contractual continuity. The study contributes a replicable, source-audited empirical methodology linking firm-level resilience performance to the sustainability outcomes of commodity-dependent supply chains under active disruption.

title: Ethical Accounting and Technology-Driven Reporting Practices: A Study of Select Indian Companies
summary: Financial reporting is a significant process through which companies communicate their financial performance and position, to investors and other stakeholders. This study examines the financial reporting and accounting practices followed by Tata Motors Ltd., Wipro Ltd., and Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd., with significance on the application of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), transparency and financial disclosures while reporting to investors and stakeholders. The study uses both quantitative and qualitative methods. The quantitative analysis is based on selected financial indicators such as Revenue, Profit After Tax (PAT), Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) and EBITDA Margin to understand and compare the financial performance of the selected companies. The qualitative part examines the nature of disclosures made in their financial reports and the extent to which accounting principles relating to transparency, reliability and accountability are reflected in their reporting practices. The study also considers the role of technology in financial reporting. The increasing use of digital reporting and analytical tools has made financial information more accessible. This can assist investors and other users of financial statements in making better- informed decisions. Based on the analysis, the study observes that Tata Motors, Wipro and Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories follow established accounting and reporting practices and provide financial information in accordance with the applicable reporting framework.

title: SAE Theory of the Company · Paper 4: Partners / SAE 公司论 第四篇: 伙伴
summary: This paper asks whether "a person has no equivalent" stops at a company's boundary. On April 24, 2013, the Rana Plaza building in Bangladesh collapsed and more than eleven hundred garment workers died; the five factories in the building made clothes for the American and EU markets. The dead were not the brands' employees; they were people on the partners' side. This paper's answer is: it does not stop; it goes all the way down the chain. A partner is another company, a construct; behind the construct are people. When a company writes oughts toward a partner, it is construct to construct; the people on the partner's side are identified separately by Institution Theory's two branches, and the rules and appeals the partner construct faces are examined separately under the Specialist Paper. A company buys what partners do, and the price falls on what is done; it does not press costs, layer by layer, into the Base Layer of the people on the partners' side; the longer the chain, the more clearly it must be written who is accountable, and accountability cannot be subcontracted away; the power-face that shows in a cooperative relation is subject to checks, and the more a partner depends on the company and the less it can get around it, the stronger the checks and the more explanation and routes of questioning the company owes it (GS10). The Bangladesh accord on fire and building safety, Germany's Supply Chain Due Diligence Act and Germany's ban on subcontracting in the meat industry show how the rule layer gives "all the way down the chain" efficacy, and also show that efficacy must be examined by the three questions. The UK Groceries Code Adjudicator's finding against Tesco and the EU's Late Payment Directive speak of paying as agreed and on time; the EU's Platform-to-Business Regulation speaks of a marketplace's rules being stated, changes announced in advance, differences in treatment of the platform's own offerings set out, and appeals having a door. Crossways Market telling sellers "you can choose not to sell here" does not answer what it was asked. Finally the paper speaks of direction: growing together. title: Duties of Directors Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 And Analysis of the Principle of Corporate Governance
summary: This paper discussed the duties of directors of companies, the principle of corporate governance and the role of directors as a board to ensuring good corporate governance. It discussed the appointment, powers, removal and rotation of directors. This research work adopted the doctrinal approach. It relied on both primary and secondary sources of information or data. Primarily, it utilizes a legal approach using primary data such as the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 and the Code of Corporate Governance for Public Companies. The secondary sources of data uitilised include textbooks, online articles in learned journals, relevant materials from the Internet, Magazines, Newspapers, other Periodicals, Dictionaries and Reports. It was found that directors are very important figures in the administration of a company and their relationship being a fiduciary one is most certainly a relationship of utmost truth and that the Board of Directors is at the very core of existence of a company. The paper concluded that despite the rich provisions of the CAMA and the Code of Corporate Governance as to the role of the directors in ensuring good corporate governance, there are still challenges in achieving this role, the paper therefore make recommendations on how to effectively monitor compliance and balance the diverse interests of all stakeholders.

title: ACCOUNTING, AUDIT, AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE MARKETING POLICY OF A FOOD-INDUSTRY ENTERPRISE: THE CASE OF NESTLÉ UKRAINE LLC
summary: The article substantiates methodological approaches to organizing the accounting and internal audit of marketing expenses of a food-industry enterprise using the example of Nestlé Ukraine LLC. It reveals the composition of marketing expenses recorded as selling expenses, including advertising and marketing communications, advertising agency services, promotion in social media and digital channels, exhibitions and promotional campaigns, trade marketing, merchandising, and logistics support for product distribution. The need for detailed analytical accounting of these expenses by the company's brand portfolio (Svitoch, Torchyn, Mivina, NESCAFÉ, KitKat) is substantiated, since their generalized reflection limits management's ability to assess the return on specific marketing investments. Problematic aspects of the current accounting system are identified: insufficient brand-level detail, difficulty in separating advertising, logistics, and trade-marketing expenses, and a weak link between accounting data and marketing analytics. It is established that over the period under study selling expenses grew significantly, reflecting substantial investment in marketing activity, yet despite rising net sales revenue the company continued to incur a net loss. A plan and program for the internal audit of marketing activity are developed, covering verification of advertising and key-brand promotion costs, digital-marketing accounting, evaluation of trade-marketing effectiveness, and analysis of marketing budget execution. A set of organizational and economic measures for improving the marketing policy is proposed, including detailed brand-level analytical accounting, introduction of the ROMI indicator, strengthened internal audit, improved management reporting, consumer-preference research, a digital advertising campaign, expanded trade-marketing programs, and staff upskilling. A cost estimate for implementing these measures is prepared, and it is shown that their implementation will increase net revenue and gross profit and reduce the net loss.

title: Unpacking the relationship between overall ESG performance and employee satisfaction: evidence of differentiated effects
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is uniformly associated with employee satisfaction or produces differentiated effects across distinct satisfaction facets. It further investigates whether organizational consensus conditions these relationships, thereby clarifying when objective ESG performance translates into more favorable employee evaluations. Design/methodology/approach The study combines firm-level ESG ratings from the Korea Corporate Governance Service with 26,072 employee reviews from JobPlanet across 117 South Korean listed firms from 2018 to 2022. Multilevel models examine the association between overall ESG performance and six employee satisfaction facets. Additional analyses test organizational consensus and visibility as firm-level moderators, together with lagged models, firm-size analyses and an alternative consensus measure based on former-employee reviews. Findings Overall ESG performance is positively associated with overall satisfaction, compensation and benefits and career advancement, but shows no average association with work-life balance, company culture or management quality. However, these relationships are contingent on organizational consensus. The ESG–satisfaction association becomes more favorable when employees hold more convergent organizational evaluations, while several relationships become negative under low consensus. Thus, the apparent null effects for some satisfaction facets conceal opposing conditional relationships. Originality/value This study moves beyond the assumption that ESG uniformly improves employee attitudes by demonstrating both facet specificity and perceptual contingency in the ESG–employee satisfaction relationship. It refines social exchange theory by showing that reciprocal responses depend on the type of employee outcome considered and the organizational perceptual context. By distinguishing the interpretive role of signaling theory from the reciprocity mechanism of social exchange theory, the study provides a more nuanced explanation of how objective ESG performance translates into employee outcomes.

title: Accidental supply chains: an exploratory study of social enterprise coordination in Australian organics recovery
summary: Purpose To explain how social enterprises coordinate circular organics recovery in regional settings where formal infrastructure is incomplete and institutional support remains thin. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, abductive multiple-case study of two Australian organics recovery arrangements, drawing on 26 semi-structured interviews, site observations, documentary sources and iterative tracing of material flows and coordination over time. Findings Circular coordination developed through four overlapping phases: initiation, stabilisation, legitimation and institutionalisation. Repeated routines and micro-infrastructure, supported by relationship-based brokerage, made recovery workable amid structural, socio-political and emergent complexity. Supply-chain championing was centralised in SoilCo and decentralised in CoffeeCos, but remained active across the full process. Greater visibility strengthened legitimacy and formalisation while also creating new scrutiny and operating burdens, including competition for previously unwanted material. Research limitations/implications The study prioritises analytical depth in two Australian organics recovery cases. Research across other materials and institutional settings could test the scope and boundary conditions of accidental supply chains. Practical implications Regional circularity requires investment in coordination and relationship-based governance, as well as low-capital storage and consolidation alongside major infrastructure. Social implications Regional organics recovery can generate locally visible environmental and community benefits by connecting waste generators with local users. Sustaining these benefits depends on trust, participation and place-based coordination across the pathway. Originality/value The article conceptualises accidental supply chains as a distinct organising mode in which deliberate local action produces a recognisable supply architecture through repeated practice without prior blueprinting.

title: Who bears the liquidity burden? Industry concentration and trade credit imbalance in supply chains
summary: Purpose This study examines how firms redistribute liquidity across supply chain partners through trade credit policies. Moving beyond aggregate working capital measures, it conceptualizes trade credit imbalance as a directional mechanism through which firms extract or extend financing within buyer–supplier–customer relationships. The study investigates how industry concentration is associated with this redistribution. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from Standard & Poor's 500 Composite Stock Price Index firms over the period 2016–2023, the study employs regression analysis to test for a nonlinear relationship between industry concentration and trade credit imbalance. It further examines the moderating role of board characteristics, namely chief executive officer (CEO) duality and board women concentration. Findings The results reveal a U-shaped relationship between industry concentration and trade credit imbalance, indicating that firms in moderately concentrated industries exhibit relatively lower imbalance compared to those in highly competitive or highly concentrated settings. Board women presence attenuates this relationship, while CEO duality shows no significant moderating effect. Practical implications The findings suggest that managers should consider industry structure when designing trade credit policies and recognize the role of board composition in influencing financially and relationally balanced decisions within supply chains. Originality/value This study introduces trade credit imbalance as a directional measure of working capital management and provides evidence of its nonlinear association with industry structure. It contributes by linking industry concentration and board composition to firms' trade credit decisions.

title: Perspectives on Health Logistics in Saudi Arabia: Progress and Challenges
summary: Saudi Arabia has identified healthcare supply chain transformation as a key component of the Health Sector Transformation Program under Vision 2030, yet evidence on these reforms remains fragmented across sectors and policy domains. Drawing on the published literature, policy documents, institutional reports, and the authors’ experience in national procurement, regulation, and public health, this perspective examines four interacting components of transformation—procurement governance, digital infrastructure, local manufacturing capacity, and emergency preparedness—and applies this framework to antimicrobial resistance. Substantial reforms have been implemented, notably centralized procurement through the National Unified Procurement Company, national digital surveillance and traceability systems, and the localization of strategic medicines such as insulin. We propose that interactions among these reforms may influence supply chain resilience, although weak public–private data integration, dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients, and limited performance evaluations prevent firm conclusions about their system-level effects. Remaining challenges include recurrent medicine shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, workforce gaps, and the limited availability of public performance indicators. The Saudi experience suggests that centralized, state-led reform should balance efficiency with redundancy, prioritize localization selectively, and build transparent performance monitoring into reforms from the outset.

title: Energy Transition Policies and Corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance Performance: Evidence from a Quasi-Natural Experiment on New Energy Demonstration Cities
summary: To examine whether a place-based energy-transition policy improves corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, we develop research adopting an interactional perspective between micro-level corporate behavior and the macro-level policy environment. Our analysis utilizes 37,817 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share firms listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen over the period 2009–2023. The empirical results are as follows. Firstly, the policy has a significantly positive effect on corporate ESG performance. Secondly, this effect is transmitted through greater environmental protection expenditure, stronger green innovation, and increased city-level credit supply. Thirdly, media attention further amplifies the policy impact. Finally, the effect is stronger among non-state-owned firms, mature-stage firms, high-carbon-intensity firms, and firms operating in less competitive markets. These findings clarify how local energy-transition initiatives shape corporate sustainability and highlight the complementary roles of environmental investment, green innovation, credit provision, and information scrutiny.

title: Unified Payments Interface (UPI): Trends and Growth in India’s Digital Economy
summary: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has emerged as a major component of India’s digital payment ecosystem, with substantial growth in transaction volume, transaction value and participating banks since its introduction. Although previous studies have examined the expansion, adoption and ecosystem of UPI, there is scope for an updated longitudinal assessment of its growth pattern and the association between bank participation and UPI transaction activity over an extended period. Against this background, the present study examines the trends and growth of UPI in India during the financial years 2016–17 to 2025–26 and analyses the association between participating banks and UPI transaction activity. The study is based on secondary data compiled from the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and other relevant published sources. Descriptive statistics, year-wise trend analysis, annual growth rate (AGR), compound annual growth rate (CAGR), and Pearson correlation are employed to analyse the data. The findings indicate a substantial increase in UPI transaction volume and value over the study period, accompanied by a considerable expansion in the number of participating banks. The correlation analysis indicates a strong positive association between bank participation and both UPI transaction volume and transaction value. The study also identifies challenges related to digital literacy, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, merchant awareness, and data privacy. The findings highlight the continued expansion of UPI and the importance of strengthening digital infrastructure, financial literacy, and payment security to support inclusive digital payment growth in India. Keywords: Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Digital Payments, Digital Economy, NPCI, Transaction Volume, Transaction Value, Participating Banks

title: Challenges Facing Facilities Management in the Automation and Digital Transformation of Private Universities
summary: Digital transformation (DT) and automation can move campus operations from reactive repair to proactive asset management, yet facilities management (FM) in private higher education still relies on manual workflows and fragmented legacy infrastructure. Aligned with Saudi Vision 2030, this study quantifies the barriers impeding DT adoption in private university FM. A questionnaire covering 40 challenges across five dimensions, derived from a structured literature review, was administered on a four-point challenge scale to facilities managers (n = 60) and IT specialists (n = 60) drawn from six private universities in three regions of Saudi Arabia. Responses were converted into a Relative Challenge Index (RCI) and ranked; agreement was assessed with Spearman’s rank correlation and item-level differences with Mann–Whitney U tests under Holm–Bonferroni correction, with robustness established by bootstrapping (B = 10,000) and by weighting-scheme and sample-size sensitivity analyses. Facilities managers ranked legacy system incompatibility (RCI = 87.08%), absent IT–FM budgets (85.83%) and hidden integration costs (84.17%) highest; IT specialists prioritized cybersecurity risks (90.42%), legacy system incompatibility (90.00%) and poor platform integration (89.58%). The two groups reported statistically indistinguishable overall burden (Wilcoxon p = 0.702; equivalent to within ±10 percentage points by a two one-sided test, p = 0.0017) but agreed only weakly on its distribution (ρ = 0.390, p = 0.013), with 22 of 40 items differing significantly after correction. The FM–IT disconnect is therefore one of attention rather than intensity, and a four-quadrant priority matrix separates 14 consensus targets from 12 contested items requiring negotiated governance.

title: Corporate Governance Characteristics and Organisational Performance in Kenya’s Export Floriculture Companies: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
summary: Corporate governance is expected to support accountability and organisational coordination, but the strength of its association with performance may vary across settings and measurement approaches. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined the relationships between leadership structure, internal control strategy, governance norms and perceived organisational performance among export floricultural companies in Kenya. Twenty companies were purposively selected for this study; 16 returned usable questionnaires, an 80% response rate. Because of item-level missingness, analytic sample sizes varied; the principal correlation and multiple-regression analyses used 14 observations. Pearson correlations between perceived performance and leadership structure (r = −.058, p = .844), internal control strategy (r = .102, p = .728) and governance norms (r = .198, p = .498) were not statistically significant. The joint regression model was also not significant, F(3, 10) = 0.350, p = .790, R² = .095, adjusted R² = −.177. Internal control strategy and governance norms were strongly correlated (r = .880, p < .001), raising a concern about construct overlap and coefficient stability. These findings do not establish that governance is unimportant; rather, the small purposive sample provides limited precision and generalisability. The study offers preliminary sector-specific evidence and identifies priorities for larger studies using multiple informants, validated measures and independently verified performance indicators.

title: Multi-Objective Constrained Deep Q-Networks for Supplier Selection and Order Allocation in Sustainable Supply Chains
summary: Abstract Sustainable sourcing requires sequential decisions that couple discrete supplier admission, integer order quantities, stochastic lead times, inventory, and competing economic, environmental, and service objectives. We formulate this setting as a preference-conditioned constrained Markov decision process with state-dependent, mixed-integer action feasibility and distributional tail-risk requirements. We develop ParetoShield-Q, a multi-objective deep Q-learning formulation that uses an augmented Chebyshev action functional over distributional cost-to-go estimates and a completion-feasibility oracle to construct executable supplier allocations. The same constrained Bellman operator jointly determines which objectives are optimized, which downstream risks are penalized, and which supplier--quantity assignments are legally selectable. We establish conditional one-step feasibility and finite-candidate Pareto-efficiency properties, and provide an evaluation protocol based on the public M5 demand data and a public supplier-attribute dataset. The study presents seven quantitative tables and eight vector figures spanning multi-objective performance, preference control, cost composition, operational feasibility, ablations, disruption response, and computational scaling. The visualizations reproduce the tabulated numerical summaries without constructing unobserved run-level training traces. Independent reproduction requires the source training runs, scenario configurations, and optimizer logs.

title: AI-Driven sustainable operations management in manufacturing supply chains: A systematic review, research gap analysis, and strategic framework for future directions
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming manufacturing supply chains by enabling intelligent decision-making, adaptive operations, and more efficient resource utilization. Its potential to advance sustainable operations management, however, extends beyond technological adoption to the organizational integration of AI capabilities into operational processes and sustainability-oriented strategies. Despite growing scholarly attention, research in this field remains fragmented across technological applications, manufacturing functions, organizational conditions, and sustainability dimensions. In particular, limited conceptual integration exists regarding how AI capabilities are translated into operational transformation and under what organizational and technological conditions such transformation generates sustainable value. To address these limitations, this study conducts a systematic literature review and structured research gap analysis of peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 1 June 2026. The review examines the intellectual evolution of the field, synthesizes dominant research themes, evaluates AI applications across manufacturing and supply chain operations, and critically assesses their implications for operational, environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The synthesis highlights an emerging shift from isolated, function-specific AI applications towards interconnected and increasingly autonomous operational ecosystems, supported by the convergence of AI with the Internet of Things (IoT), digital twins, cyber-physical systems, and advanced analytics. These developments create opportunities for predictive and prescriptive decision-making, intelligent production planning, predictive maintenance, quality optimization, resource efficiency, supply chain visibility, and disruption management. Nevertheless, the realization of these benefits remains contingent upon organizational readiness, digital infrastructure maturity, data quality, workforce capabilities, effective governance, and the alignment of technological investments with sustainability priorities. The review further identifies persistent theoretical, methodological, technological, organizational, and empirical gaps, particularly concerning human–AI collaboration, implementation scalability, algorithmic accountability, sustainability trade-offs, and the assessment of long-term performance outcomes. Building on these insights, the study develops an AI-Driven Sustainable Operations Management Strategic Framework that integrates AI technological capabilities, organizational and digital enablers, AI-enabled operational transformation mechanisms, sustainability-oriented governance, and multidimensional performance outcomes. By connecting technological potential with organizational transformation and sustainability performance, the proposed framework provides an integrative conceptual foundation for understanding AI-enabled sustainable value creation across manufacturing supply chains. It also establishes a structured agenda for future research and offers strategic implications for manufacturing organizations and policymakers seeking to advance responsible AI adoption, strengthen operational resilience, and achieve sustainable long-term competitiveness.

title: Pengaruh Carbon Emission Disclosure Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Dengan Good Corporate Governance Sebagai Variabel Moderasi (Studi pada Perusahaan Sektor Basic Materials yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2022–2025)
summary: The launch of IDXCarbon in September 2023 and the start of international carbon trading in January 2025 have made Carbon Emission Disclosure (CED) increasingly relevant to investor valuation. This study analyzes the effect of CED on firm value and the role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) as both a direct predictor and a moderator of this relationship among Basic Materials companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2025. Using purposive sampling, the sample comprises 64 companies (256 observations). Firm value is measured by Tobin’s Q, CED by an 18-item checklist, and GCG by the proportion of independent commissioners, with ROA and leverage as control variables. The data are analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis with a Random Effects Model (Panel EGLS), selected through the Chow and Hausman tests, and robustness is examined through FEM comparison and robust standard errors. The results show that CED has no significant effect on firm value (β = 0.370; p = 0.555), GCG has no significant effect (β = −0.608; p = 0.405), and GCG does not moderate the CED–firm value relationship (β= 0.208; p = 0.882), classifying GCG as a homologiser moderator. These findings are consistent across all robustness tests and suggest that the Indonesian capital market has not yet priced carbon emission information during the early phase of its carbon market. Firms should therefore improve the quality and verification of emission disclosures, while regulators should standardize disclosure requirements and strengthen the effectiveness of independent commissioner oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in IT Management and Business Management: A Critical Literature Review
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation now feature prominently in discussions about business strategy and information technology. However, simply introducing an AI tool does not guarantee better results. Organisations need to connect technology decisions with business priorities, prepare reliable data and infrastructure, develop staff skills, manage risks, and fit new tools into everyday work. This review brings together selected literature around five related themes: 1) digital transformation as organisational change; 2) AI readiness and organisational capabilities; 3) IT governance and strategic alignment; 4) implementation challenges and responsible use; and 5) the measurement of business value. It draws on perspectives such as the Technology–Organisation–Environment framework, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities, IT governance, and technology-acceptance models. Across these themes, one point stands out: readiness, governance, implementation, and value are closely connected and are best examined as parts of the same management process. The literature review paper offers a provisional framework and propositions for future research.
