title: Disaggregated ESG Pillars and Firm Value: The Moderating Role of Board Diversity in European Listed Companies
summary: Abstract Purpose : This study examines the individual effects of the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) pillars on firm value and whether board diversity moderates these relationships, addressing inconsistent findings in the ESG–performance literature. Design/Methodology/Approach : Using a dynamic panel of European listed companies (2014–2023), the study applies a two-step system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimator to control for endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, and performance persistence. Board diversity is measured with a composite index derived via principal component analysis (PCA), and interaction terms test moderating effects. Findings : ESG pillars, assessed independently, have no significant direct effect on firm value. However, board diversity significantly moderates the ESG–performance relationship, particularly for the environmental and social pillars. Robustness checks using an alternative Tobin’s Q specification confirm the results. Practical Implications : ESG initiatives do not enhance performance on their own; they require governance structures capable of interpreting and executing sustainability strategies. Firms and policymakers should therefore prioritize board diversity to strengthen ESG integration. Theoretical Implications : The study contributes to stakeholder, agency, and upper echelon theories by showing that the ESG–performance link is contingent on board characteristics, challenging the assumption of universal ESG benefits and supporting a contingency-based perspective. Originality/Value : By disaggregating ESG pillars and modelling board diversity as a moderator within a dynamic panel framework, the study clarifies when and how ESG practices influence firm value, and strengthens methodological robustness through GMM estimation and alternative performance measures.

title: Inverse Fintech: Research Prospectus, Version 1.1: Physical Asset Depreciation, Information Appreciation and Institutional Value Creation
summary: This research prospectus invites independent academic collaboration on Inverse Fintech, an asset-first approach to financial inclusion in which access to productive physical assets precedes, rather than follows, access to credit. It sets out the concept's core propositions, the open research questions it raises, and a proposed empirical setting: a pilot in Kenya implemented by WeSail.Green. Partner institutions are invited to co-design the research, including a planned household survey (approx. 500 households), and to pursue questions beyond the implementing organisation's own purposes. Research partners are expected to retain full methodological and publication independence. The prospectus builds on two earlier works by the author: the definition paper (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24046147) and the explanatory paper (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24056786).

title: Green Accounting Disclosure in State-Owned Bank
summary: Research Aims: This study aims to analyze 1) The mean difference test of green accounting disclosure in state-owned bank before and after joining Danantara Indonesia. 2) How banking companies disclose sustainability information in annual reports in accordance with applicable regulation. Design/methodology/approach: This study employs mixed-method approach with combining quantitative and qualitative approach. A quantitative method involving a test for the difference in means, conducted using Microsoft Excel. The data comprises the green accounting of state-owned banks e.g. PT. Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. (BNI), PT. Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk. (Mandiri), PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. (BTN), and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. A qualitative approach using content analysis includes identifying sustainability standards used by banking companies in their annual reports. Research Findings: Quantitative approach findings indicate that there is no difference in the average level of green accounting disclosure before and after the launch of Danantara among state-owned banks. This suggests consistency in green accounting reporting across the banks. Qualitative approach findings indicate that PT BNI and PT BTN reported 71%. PT Bank Mandiri reported 51%, and PT BRI reported 43% from available standards. Theoretical Contribution/Originality: This research intends to examine phenomena in green banking disclosure and contribute to legitimacy theory.

title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
summary: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built on Refinitiv and MSCI ratings, and pass VaR backtests at 95% coverage. The results support text-based ESG modeling as an alternative to vendor-rating-based approaches, particularly where downside risk management and traceable explanation are jointly required.

title: Metric vs. Syntactic Saturation: A Fare Algebra Audit of Heron's Method
summary: Classical numerical analysis treats floating-point error as a gradual accumulation of rounding mistakes. The Monkey Business Arithmetic Spectator Pipeline (MBP) models numeric representations as algebraic environments with specific capacities and incapacities. A central question is whether the saturation of a finite environment is a single phenomenon or a bifurcated one. This paper presents an exact-arithmetic audit of Heron's method for the square root of 2, revealing two distinct structural failure modes. Syntactic Saturation occurs when an operation lacks the moveset to construct a value (e.g., nested irrationals), triggering a geometric Apeirogon limit - the point where the finite environment shatters while attempting to simulate a continuous curve. Metric Saturation (a Representational Lock) occurs when a legal rational trajectory falls permanently into a float's rounding interval. The audit shows Heron's method triggers the Metric Lock without reaching the Apeirogon limit. Furthermore, exact auditing reveals a round-to-even tie that splits the single-cast and float-pipeline trajectories by exactly one ULP, quantifying the geometric cost of intermediate rounding.Status: Technical Research Note (v0.5). The exact rational fractions and 1-ULP tie data were generated via a closed computational run (Z.ai GLM) acting as an independent auditor against the public fare-audit engine. The engine and broad test suites are available on GitHub.

title: Teori Keagenan dalam Penelitian Akuntansi dan Auditing 2024–2026
summary: Penelitian ini memetakan dan mengevaluasi bagaimana teori agensi telah diterapkan dalam penelitian akuntansi dan audit yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2024 dan 2026. Sesuai dengan protokol PRISMA 2020, pencarian di Scopus yang dilakukan pada 17 Oktober 2026 menghasilkan 103 artikel akses terbuka, dimana 23 diantaranya memenuhi kriteria inklusi dan disintesis secara naratif. Pemantauan mendominasi literatur, muncul dalam 14 studi, sementara ikatan diuji secara langsung hanya dalam dua studi, dan tidak ada satupun studi yang dilakukan di Indonesia. Sintesis ini mengelompokkan bukti ke dalam lima tema dan menunjukkan bahwa beberapa temuan yang tampaknya bertentangan dengan teori agensi dapat dijelaskan dengan lebih baik oleh ukuran sampel yang kecil, trade-off antara kualitas audit dan ketepatan waktu, serta masalah agensi diantara para pemantau itu sendiri. Berdasarkan evaluasi ini, penelitian ini mengembangkan kerangka kerja integratif yang menghubungkan sumber-sumber konflik agensi, pemantauan, pembentukan ikatan, dan mekanisme insentif, serta hasil akuntansi, yang dimoderasi oleh konteks kelembagaan. Lima proposisi yang dapat diuji diturunkan dari kerangka kerja tersebut, dengan perhatian khusus pada kepemilikan terkonsentrasi, dewan direksi dua tingkat, dan regulasi komite audit di Indonesia

title: AI-Enabled FinTech Services: Examining Consumer Trust, Security, and Behavioural Intentions an Empirical Investigation into the Insurance Sector in India
summary: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and financial technology (FinTech) has transformed the operational architecture of India's insurance industry, redefining how consumers interact with insurers across underwriting, claims settlement, and personalised advisory services. This study investigates the interplay between consumer trust, perceived security, and behavioural intentions toward AI-enabled FinTech services among insurance customers in India. Anchored in an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) integrated with the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the research examines how perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, data privacy concerns, algorithmic transparency, and institutional trust collectively shape adoption behaviour. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 412 policyholders across metropolitan and tier-II cities using a structured questionnaire measured on a five-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, and multiple regression using SPSS. Findings reveal that consumer trust (β = 0.412, p < 0.001) and perceived security (β = 0.338, p < 0.001) exert the strongest positive influence on behavioural intentions to adopt AI-driven insurance services. Data privacy apprehension emerged as a significant negative moderator, while algorithmic transparency substantially enhanced trust formation. The study concludes that Indian insurers must prioritise transparent AI governance, robust cybersecurity frameworks, and human–AI hybrid service models to accelerate consumer acceptance. These insights contribute theoretically by contextualising trust–security dynamics within an emerging economy and offer practical guidance to insurers, regulators such as IRDAI, and policymakers seeking to foster responsible AI adoption in the Indian insurance landscape.

title: Tax evasion at the top of the income distribution
summary: We study tax evasion at the top of the U.S. income distribution using micro-data from audits and enforcement initiatives. Leveraging enforcement that revealed noncompliance, we find that recent individual random audit data fail to capture sophisticated evasion via offshore accounts and pass-through businesses. Consequently, estimates based solely on these data under-state evasion by the highest-income Americans. We construct new distributional estimates of US noncompliance. Circa 2006–2013, accounting for sophisticated evasion (holding estimated non-sophisticated evasion fixed) increases the share of unreported income belonging to the top 1% of the distribution by 9 to 33 percentage points.

title: Advancing the Sustainable Development Goals in E7 Economies: The Role of ECON ‐ ESG Governance in Mitigating the Environmental Effects of Urbanization
summary: ABSTRACT Rapid urbanization, industrialization, and rising energy demand intensify environmental pressures in E7 economies and complicate progress toward key Sustainable Development Goals. This study examines the effects of urbanization, energy transition, trade openness, technological development, and Environmental, Social, Governance, and Economic Sustainability (ECON‐ESG) performance on greenhouse gas emissions in E7 countries over 2000–2023, while also assessing the moderating role of ECON‐ESG in the urbanization–environment relationship through the URB × ECON‐ESG interaction. Panel‐corrected standard errors (PCSE) are employed as the main estimator, fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) are used for robustness analysis, and wavelet coherence captures time‐ and frequency‐varying ECON‐ESG–GHG dynamics. The results show that urbanization, trade openness, and technological development are associated with higher GHG emissions, whereas stronger ECON‐ESG performance is associated with lower emissions. The energy‐transition effect is sensitive to model specification and estimator choice, indicating that its environmental contribution is not uniform across specifications. The interaction term is negative, providing evidence that stronger ECON‐ESG performance can attenuate the adverse environmental effect of urbanization, while wavelet results reveal heterogeneous but generally stronger inverse ECON‐ESG–GHG co‐movement over medium‐ and long‐run horizons. By combining a multidimensional ECON‐ESG framework with total GHG emissions and an urbanization moderation perspective, the study offers policy implications for sustainable urban planning, environmentally oriented innovation, cleaner trade structures, effective energy transition, and integrated sustainability governance in emerging economies.

title: Оцінювання повноти та якості розкриття екологічної інформації у ESG-звітності підприємств гірничо-металургійного комплексу
summary: Стаття присвячена розробленню методичного підходу до комплексного оцінювання повноти та якості розкриття еколо- гічної інформації у корпоративній звітності підприємств гірничо-металургійного комплексу відповідно до Європейських стандартів звітності зі сталого розвитку (ESRS E1 – E5). Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням вимог до корпо- ративної прозорості внаслідок ухвалення Директиви (ЄС) 2022/2464 (CSRD), значним екологічним впливом гірничо-мета- лургійного виробництва та обмеженою порівнюваністю наявних ESG-даних. Для проведення контент-аналізу сформовано систему з 30 індикаторів, об’єднаних у п’ять тематичних блоків відповідно до стандартів ESRS E1 «Зміна клімату», E2 «Забруднення», E3 «Водні та морські ресурси», E4 «Біорізноманіття та екосистеми» та E5 «Використання ресурсів і цир- кулярна економіка». Для кількісної оцінки розроблено шестирівневу кумулятивну шкалу від 0 до 5 балів, яка розмежовує відсутність інформації, декларативне розкриття та повне кількісне й верифіковане представлення даних. Інформаційну основу дослідження становили дев’ять інтегрованих річних звітів, звітів зі сталого розвитку та кліматичних звітів компаній Metinvest, Ferrexpo та Interpipe за 2022 – 2024 рр., за якими здійснено 270 індикаторних оцінювань. За результатами роз- раховано часткові індекси за кожним стандартом ESRS та інтегральний індекс екологічної прозорості. Найвище значення ІЕП у 2024 р. отримав Interpipe (68,4 %), друге місце посіла Ferrexpo (65,6 %), показник Metinvest становив 56,6 %. Жоден зі звітів не досяг рівня понад 80 %. Найповніше розкритими виявилися блоки ESRS E1 та ESRS E5 (по 68,9 %), найменш повно ESRS E4 (49,6 %), що свідчить про недостатнє висвітлення впливів на біорізноманіття та екосистеми. Отримані результати можуть використовуватися підприємствами, аудиторами, інвесторами й органами публічного управління для порівняльної оцінки якості екологічних розкриттів та підготовки даних до незалежного підтвердження.

title: Pengaruh Pemahaman AI Dan Inovasi Digital Serta Literasi Pasar Modal Terhadap Niat Berwirausaha Digital Dengan Efikasi Diri Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
summary: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital capital markets creates new business opportunities, yet little is known about how students' understanding of both domains shapes their digital entrepreneurial intention. This study examines the effect of understanding of AI and digital innovation and of capital market literacy on digital entrepreneurial intention, with self-efficacy as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey of 153 students attending a public lecture was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The measurement model met the criteria for convergent validity, reliability, and discriminant validity. Understanding of AI and digital innovation (β = 0.480) and capital market literacy (β = 0.325) had positive and significant effects on self-efficacy. Self-efficacy had the strongest effect on digital entrepreneurial intention (β = 0.526) and mediated the effects of both independent variables. Capital market literacy also had a significant direct effect (β = 0.286), whereas understanding of AI and digital innovation had no direct effect (β = 0.099; p = 0.238), so its influence operates fully through self-efficacy. The model explains 69.8% of the variance in digital entrepreneurial intention. The findings imply that public lectures and entrepreneurship education should build students' self-belief rather than only transfer knowledge.

title: Assessing the Role of Digital Technologies for Health Financing (DTHF) in Strengthening Public Health Financing Systems in Nigeria
summary: Abstract Background Nigeria's health financing system remains heavily dependent on out-of-pocket payments, leaving large segments of the population, particularly those in rural and informal-sector settings, exposed to catastrophic health expenditure. The 2022 National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) Act mandated universal health insurance enrollment, intensifying the need for financing mechanisms capable of reaching populations that traditional cash-based systems have struggled to serve. Digital Technologies for Health Financing (DTHF), including mobile money platforms, digital payment gateways, and API-driven interoperability between insurers, telecommunications providers, and FinTech companies, have emerged as a potentially transformative strategy, yet empirical evidence on their implementation and the operational, behavioural, and regulatory factors shaping their effectiveness in Nigeria remains limited. Methods This qualitative descriptive study used semi-structured Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) with 17 senior personnel and technical experts drawn from national and state health insurance agencies, Health Maintenance Organizations, FinTech companies, and payment service providers across Lagos, Oyo, Ondo, and the Federal Capital Territory. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase reflexive thematic analysis framework, with trustworthiness established through Lincoln and Guba's criteria of credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability. Results Six themes emerged: digital transformation as an equity and revenue modernization vehicle; ecosystem interoperability and multi-sectoral integration; operational constraints and systemic enablers; trust, governance, and regulatory compliance architecture; reminder systems and automatic renewals; and scaling digital health financing for universal health coverage. Participants viewed DTHF as simultaneously expanding access for underserved populations and strengthening financial transparency, but implementation was constrained by infrastructural fragility, workforce turnover, fragmented interoperability standards, and an evolving regulatory landscape. Behavioural design of reminders and automatic renewals emerged as an important, underutilized lever for improving enrollee retention. Conclusion DTHF holds substantial promise for advancing Universal Health Coverage in Nigeria, but its impact is bounded by institutional, infrastructural, regulatory, and behavioural factors beyond the technology itself. Strengthening these underlying systems, alongside continued technological investment, is essential for sustainable scale-up.

title: ACCOUNTING OF INCOME AND EXPENSES AS A BASIS FOR INCREASING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS COMPANIES
summary: It is substantiated that the specifics of the activities of companies operating in the field of electronic communications significantly affect the accounting practice of income and expenses. This necessitates the need to conduct a comparative analysis between the costs incurred and the results of the activity. Under such conditions, accounting should be rationally organized in order to avoid negative factors. Summarizing the results of the study, it should be noted that despite the difficult economic conditions and military actions, telecommunications companies continue to work effectively and remain the leaders of the modern services market. The telecommunications services market is quite specific, so it needs to be constantly studied. A specific feature should be considered that the enterprises of this sphere are quite multifunctional and are involved in providing services to a specific consumer at a certain stage of the entire production process, and significant volumes of activity are subject to state regulation, which is regulated at the state level (in particular, this is a subscription fee, rental of telecommunications cable ducts). The issue of changing demand in this market requires special attention. This will make it possible to predict changes in demand, quickly respond to them and qualitatively satisfy the needs for modern types of services. Competition in the telecommunications services market encourages companies to work on reducing the cost of services by reducing costs and introducing a model that best meets modern challenges and is based on ensuring the cost reduction of mobile communications and the Internet, as well as developing activities to introduce the latest technologies with investment, which will contribute to increasing income. An important task for all telecommunications operators, without exception, should be to create favorable conditions that ensure the rapid attraction of funds for the development of the industry in order to implement the planned long-term projects. Bringing the quality of service provision to international standards contributes to increasing revenues and strengthening the competitiveness of telecommunications companies.

title: External knowledge processing in the fuzzy front end: functional perspectives, capability interdependencies and coordination interfaces
summary: Purpose This study examines how knowledge identification capability (KIC), knowledge acquisition capability (KAC) and knowledge sharing capability (KSC) are enacted from different functional positions during the fuzzy front end (FFE) of innovation, and how participants describe the interfaces through which these knowledge-processing activities connect. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive, multiple-case design and a Gioia-inspired analytical procedure. It draws on 48 expert interviews with senior professionals working in R&D, innovation, consumer intelligence and supply chain roles across eight FMCG and technology organisations. Findings The findings indicate that KIC, KAC and KSC are connected through overlap, iteration and reciprocal feedback rather than operating as an exclusively linear sequence. Participants described differentiated functional contributions, with R&D providing technical interpretation, Consumer intelligence framing behavioural relevance, supply chain contributing supplier and feasibility knowledge, and innovation facilitating translation and integration. The sampled FMCG accounts particularly emphasised signal expiry and timely insight translation, whereas technology accounts more frequently highlighted technical complexity and cross-functional interpretation. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on functionally situated managerial accounts and do not establish complete firm-level configurations or objective innovation-performance effects. Future research should use multi-function, longitudinal and project-level designs to assess whether the reported coordination patterns recur across organisations and sectors. Practical implications The study provides a diagnostic framework for identifying knowledge-processing bottlenecks, including identification without translation, acquisition without prioritisation, sharing without interpretive capacity, asynchronous activation and functional gatekeeping. Originality/value The study's originality lies in showing how established knowledge-processing capabilities are described from different functional positions and how participants report reciprocal and temporal interfaces among these activities during the FFE.

title: The Relationship between Skills Development, Internship Programs and Accounting Graduates’ Employability in Malaysia
summary: Upon entering the workforce, accounting graduates in Malaysia face significant challenges, including a slight decline in graduate employability from 90.2% in 2022 to 89.8% in 2023. This study examines how skills development (technology and interpersonal skills) and internship programs affect the employability of Malaysian accounting graduates. Grounded in Human Capital Theory, this study uses a quantitative design and an online survey distributed to accounting graduates across Malaysia. The study used SPSS to analyse a final sample of 390 valid responses. The study found that employees had a high level of technical and experiential preparedness. While technology skills, interpersonal skills, and internship programs are strongly and positively associated with graduate employability, interestingly, interpersonal skills exhibited the strongest predictive contribution. These findings show that while technology competencies and hands-on internship experience are essential in the digital era, interpersonal soft skills primarily drive graduate marketability. Higher education institutions (HEIs) must proactively reform accounting curricula, in collaboration with professional bodies, to integrate advanced digital technologies, communication workshops, and structured internship models.

title: Perceived ESG Practices and Pro‐Environmental Behavior in Hotels: Employee Satisfaction and Well‐Being as Sequential Mediating Mechanisms for Environmental Engagement
summary: ABSTRACT Improving environmental performance is a strategic priority for resource‐intensive service industries such as hospitality. This study examines how employees' perceptions of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices are associated with employee‐driven pro‐environmental behavior. Drawing on an integrated framework of social identity theory and signaling theory, we explain how organizational‐level ESG signals become psychologically salient to employees and are linked to organizational citizenship behavior for the environment (OCBE). Job satisfaction and employee well‐being are conceptualized as cognitive‐attitudinal and affective mechanisms through which ESG perceptions are associated with pro‐environmental engagement. Survey data from 269 hotel employees in Taiwan were analyzed using PLS‐SEM and multigroup analysis. The results indicate that perceived ESG practices are positively associated with job satisfaction, employee well‐being, and OCBE. Employee well‐being emerges as the more conceptually distinct and empirically stable mediator linked to OCBE, whereas the role of job satisfaction should be interpreted cautiously because the original job satisfaction items were conditioned on ESG implementation. The sequential pathway from ESG practices to job satisfaction, employee well‐being, and OCBE is statistically consistent with the proposed model but should not be interpreted as definitive causal evidence. Multigroup analysis reveals no statistically significant path differences across tenure groups, suggesting that the proposed relationships are broadly stable across employees with different tenure levels. Overall, the findings position ESG as a credible institutional signal associated with environmental citizenship through employee psychological pathways.

title: Sustainability in Retreat: Institutional Pressures and Strategic Nondisclosure
summary: ABSTRACT Recent evidence suggests that some firms deliberately undercommunicate their sustainability achievements (‘greenhushing’) while continuing to invest in sustainability, especially in controversy‐prone environments. This study sets out to (i) explore how ESG controversies reshape firms' ESG disclosure strategies by inducing greenhushing, (ii) examine how corporate visibility conditions the persistence of strategic underdisclosure and (iii) assess how a contested institutional environment shapes these responses over time. To do so, a panel of 76 NYSE‐ and NASDAQ‐listed firms over the 2020–2024 period is employed, comprising and greenhushing is computed as the negative gap between ESG disclosure and performance. Results show that greenhushing intensifies over time and that corporate visibility moderates the effect of past ESG controversies. Controversies reinforce underdisclosure among less visible firms, while as visibility increases the association weakens and turns negative among the most visible firms, indicating stronger constraints on sustained underdisclosure. The findings provide evidence of greenhushing as a disclosure‐related strategy, showing that ESG controversies can influence it and that visibility conditions firm's response. For investors and rating providers, low disclosure is not a reliable signal of weak performance in contested environments, because assessment frameworks based on reported information may reward visibility rather than substance; for managers, the viability of reduced communication depends on how intensively the firm is monitored; for regulators, mandatory baseline indicators can limit the information loss that greenhushing produces. The study clarifies when firms respond to ESG shocks with silence rather than transparency and highlights the role of visibility and stakeholder salience in shaping ESG disclosure.

title: Beyond Logos: Teaching Persuasion to Accounting Professionals Through the ELEVATE Framework
summary: Accounting education emphasizes technical proficiency but addresses persuasion only nominally, leaving professionals able to reach a correct conclusion yet underprepared to secure stakeholder acceptance. This integrative literature review synthesizes Aristotle’s rhetorical appeals, Cicero’s five canons, and seven contemporary research traditions into a teaching framework, ELEVATE, built on seven communication practices. Each practice is mapped to a rhetorical appeal, linked to an established research tradition, and illustrated with worked accounting examples. Organized as a sequence from trust to action, ELEVATE offers business communication educators a theoretically grounded approach to teaching persuasion to accounting practitioners and students. The framework awaits empirical validation.

title: Large language model agents in watershed environmental response: a hypothesis-and-theory framework for the cognitive orchestration layer
summary: Introduction Watershed environmental governance increasingly combines dense sensing infrastructure with institutions whose attention, authority, and coordination capacity remain limited. We develop the cognitive orchestration layer as a theory-building concept for examining how large language model (LLM)-based agents may connect sensing, assessment, decision advice, institutional response, and feedback without displacing domain models or public authority. Methods The Agentic Framework for Watershed Governance (AFWG) specifies three enabling pathways, three institutional interfaces, and four propositions. A purposively selected set of eight publicly documented cases is used to illustrate functional configurations, source limitations, and research gaps; it is not a systematic review or empirical evaluation. Results The cases document sensing, assessment, and decision-support functions, but do not establish improved decision quality, sustained institutional use, environmental outcomes, or agent-executed response closure. MAESTRO is retained as an adjacent-domain design illustration, not an existence proof of full-loop closure: human authorization remains necessary, and its reported performance has not been independently replicated. Discussion Transfer to watershed governance is plausible only where domain models remain authoritative, outputs carry provenance and uncertainty, named officials retain authority to authorize consequential actions, and institutional audit and failure handling are built into deployment. AFWG therefore offers a bounded conceptual framework and a falsifiable research agenda, rather than a claim that agents have already closed the watershed response loop.

title: THE IMPACT OF IPSAS COMPLIANCE ON FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE AND REPORTING QUALITY IN PUBLIC UNIVERSITIES IN RIVERS AND BAYELSA STATES, NIGERIA.
summary: This study investigated public sector accounting standards adoption and quality of financial reporting in higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa States, Nigeria. The study adopted survey research design. The study population consisted of all public higher institutions in both states and a sample size of three hundred and twenty (320) was utilized for the study. Primary and secondary sources of data were employed while univariate and multivariate analysis were used for data analysis. The multivariate analysis revealed that Pre – and Post- IPSAS adoption has no significant difference in the financial reporting of relevance while faithful representation, understandability, timeliness, verifiability and comparability has significant differences in the Pre- and Post-IPSAS adoption periods in the higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa State. The study concluded that Pre- and Post-IPSAS periods has no significant influence with relevance of higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa States; Both Pre- and Post-IPSAS adoption period has significant difference in influencing faith representation of higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa States; Both Pre- and Post-IPSAS adoption period has significant difference in influencing understandability of higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa States; Both Pre- and Post-IPSAS adoption period has significant difference in influencing timeliness of higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa States; and both Pre- and Post-IPSAS adoption period has significant difference in influencing verifiability of higher institutions in Rivers and Bayelsa State. Hence the study recommended amongst others that public sector entities should adopt both Pre-IPSAS and Post-IPSAS principles in preparing financial reporting quality in term of faithful representation because this study affirmed that both Pre and Post IPSA has significant difference in the financial reporting in term of faithful representation.
